title.rendered: Missing planes, missing billions: Residents demand answers over alleged N50bn ‘Ebonyi Air’ purchase

content.rendered:
Six months after Governor Francis Nwifuru publicly announced the purchase of three aircraft under the “Ebonyi Air” initiative, neither planes nor an official accounting of the N50bn reportedly spent have surfaced, sparking an outcry from the state’s residents, reports EDWARD NNACHI

The announcement by the Ebonyi State Government six months ago that it had procured three aircraft under its Ebonyi Air Initiative was widely welcomed in some quarters as a major step toward creating jobs, attracting investment, and boosting the state’s economy.

However, six months later, allegations surrounding the alleged disappearance of the N50bn reportedly earmarked for the acquisition of the aircraft, the government’s silence over the project, and the absence of any official update on the whereabouts of the aircraft or the status of the deal have continued to generate reactions among political observers and residents within and outside Ebonyi State.

Rather than delivering the promised economic benefits, including increased employment opportunities and investment, the project has become the subject of growing public scrutiny. Critics, including opposition figures, social media commentators, and some aviation analysts, have questioned the transparency of the initiative and are calling on the state government to provide a detailed account of the project and clarify the status of the aircraft acquisition.

Apparently following the example of neighbouring Enugu State, whose governor, Dr. Peter Mbah, launched Enugu Air in July 2025, Ebonyi State Governor Francis Nwifuru announced on January 1, 2026, that his administration had procured three aircraft.

Delivering his New Year address during a statewide broadcast from Abakaliki, the governor said the aircraft would arrive in the state before the end of January 2026.

He said, “Reliable air transport makes it easier for investors to do business, for professionals to move in and out of the state, and for our people to connect with other parts of the country and beyond.

“Ebonyi Air will support business growth, encourage tourism, and reduce the time and cost of travel. It will also strengthen Ebonyi’s position as a state that is ready to engage with the wider economy and attract new opportunities.

“By improving connectivity, we are creating conditions that support trade, investment, and job creation, while making our state more accessible and competitive.”

As of Wednesday, July 1, 2026 — six months after the announcement — the whereabouts of the aircraft and the status of the funds reportedly allocated for their purchase remain unclear, with many residents calling on the government to provide answers.

On Wednesday, social media commentator and public affairs analyst Nwoba Nwoba, in a post on his Facebook page, questioned the fate of the aircraft, describing them as “unseen purchased aircraft” and raising concerns over what he alleged to be a lack of transparency in the execution of the project.

Reacting to the development, Nwoba alleged that N50bn had been earmarked and released by the Ebonyi State Government in August 2025 for the establishment of Ebonyi Air.

According to him, the funds were allegedly entrusted to an individual from Isu in Onicha Local Government Area of the state, popularly known as “Mmiri,” to acquire aircraft for the proposed airline.

He claimed, “N50bn was earmarked and released by the current Ebonyi State Government for the acquisition of aircraft in August 2025 for the setting up of Ebonyi Air. The money was released to a young man from Isu, Onicha LGA of the state who is doing street business in Malaysia and popularly called Mmiri. He went to China to buy five pre-owned aircraft for the State Government. He returned and told the governor that he fell into the wrong hands and was scammed. He didn’t buy even one aeroplane. The N50 billion was gone just like that.

“Ask about the man called Mmiri in Isu. Just inquire about him. How could Mmiri play this fast one without the knowledge of the governor? Was it possible? Imagine awarding a contract of this nature to a street hustler in Malaysia just because he gave you financial support in 2022. Very unfortunate.”

Nwoba further alleged that the failed transaction was responsible for the government’s inability to launch the proposed airline.

He said, “That was how Gov. Nwifuru wasted Ebonyi people’s N50 billion last year on one failed deal. That’s why he didn’t float the airline any longer. This is a calamity you want me to praise? N50 billion is capable of bringing back many Abakaliki indigenes doing menial jobs in other states and empowering them with skills after proper training. This is the second time I’m making this revelation. The first was in October last year when it allegedly happened.”

Another social media commentator, Prince Anyigor Methuselah Maduabuchi, also questioned the alleged disappearance of the billions, arguing that it was economically unwise for the state government to venture into the airline business in the first place.

Speaking with The PUNCH on Wednesday, Maduabuchi said the money could have been better invested in sectors capable of stimulating the state’s economy.

He said, “First, it is economically unwise to think of purchasing aircraft worth N50bn for a poor state like Ebonyi. The governor publicly stated on New Year’s Day that the aircraft would arrive in Ebonyi within two weeks. Yet, from January till now, there has been no official update. I believe the governor owes the people an explanation.”

He argued that investing the funds in agriculture would have yielded greater economic benefits.

“The N50bn would have done remarkably well if invested in agriculture, considering that about 90 per cent of Ebonyi people depend on farming for survival. It would have improved the state’s economy and increased government revenue if deployed as grants or empowerment programmes for farmers.

“Alternatively, investing the funds in healthcare, such as establishing a state-owned university teaching hospital, would not only create employment opportunities but also improve healthcare delivery.”

Also speaking, aviation analyst Anthony Okechukwu described the proposed investment in the airline business as economically questionable, arguing that the aviation industry is highly technical and capital intensive.

According to him, many government-owned airlines are established for political rather than commercial reasons.

He said, “Most state investments in airline businesses are largely politically motivated. Many governors want to own either an airport or an airline to score political points and demonstrate that they are delivering on infrastructure.

“Meanwhile, an aircraft is not something you buy off the shelf like a car. In fact, more than half of the aircraft operating worldwide are leased, either through dry leases or wet leases.”

Explaining the difference, Okechukwu said a dry lease involves leasing only the aircraft, with the operator providing pilots, cabin crew, maintenance, insurance, fuel, operational control and regulatory approvals.

“The aircraft usually operates under the Air Operator Certificate of the airline leasing it and carries that airline’s branding,” he said.

He explained that a wet lease — also known as an ACMI lease — includes the aircraft, crew, maintenance and insurance provided by the lessor.

According to him, “These are usually the arrangements adopted by airlines seeking to establish sustainable operations.”

Okechukwu maintained that if the Ebonyi State Government genuinely intended to establish an airline, it should first have engaged aviation professionals and develop a viable business model.

“So, the narrative that a state government handed over N50bn to a single businessman sounds unusual. Aviation is a highly specialised industry that is best managed by professionals rather than politicians,” he said.

Commenting on the development, the Chairman of the Social Democratic Party in Ebonyi State, Dr. Kingsley Agbor, condemned both the airport and aircraft projects, describing them as a wasteful and imprudent use of taxpayers’ money.

He said, “Well, for me, the case of Ebonyi State and its governance is that of ‘Oh! Help us God.’ More worrisome is that most public figures whose voices would have kept the government in check are today rather in bed with the same government.

“Who, in his right senses, will conjure an airport for Ebonyi State in the first place, considering that Enugu Airport is just 45 minutes away from Abakaliki? More still, Enugu Airport is not even functioning up to 60 per cent capacity. I have come to the conclusion that these humongous projects are simply means and ways to siphon public funds.

“So, if N50bn earmarked for the purchase of aircraft is having stories around it, then its fate remains the same as we have seen before with this government and previous governments in the state.”

The SDP chairman, who lamented the selective justice of the nation’s anti-graft agencies, said the only option left was to prosecute those found culpable in the alleged shoddy deal.

“The anti-graft agencies of today are different from the one we had under President Obasanjo. The one of today is the attack dog of the APC government. So, none of my recommendations will mean anything. However, if it were under Obasanjo, I would have recommended that everyone linked to that N50bn be arrested for questioning. The governor, due to his immunity, can be spared until the day he hands over power. Fair trial would be commenced publicly, and those found culpable would be handed very stringent jail terms, including firing squad. This way, lessons will be learned and public office holders will resist taking what is not lawfully theirs.”

He added, “N50bn is so much money that if left in the hands of a competent administrator, it would change the poverty fortunes of Ebonyi State. At least five to ten industries can be established with such funds, and the multiplier effects will help change the economy of the state for the better. It can help build light rail systems to link all the 13 local government areas of the state to the capital, Abakaliki, with the multiplier effects reaching over 80 percent of our people. In the same way, jobs will be created and revenues generated for the state. But like I said, these people do not think of what will develop the state. All they think about are projects that will create avenues for them to loot public funds.”

The 2027 Labour Party governorship candidate in Ebonyi State, Eze Splendour, also condemned the development and called for the prosecution of those allegedly involved.

He said, “To be candid, I am very sad over the alleged reckless and corrupt aviation transaction by the Ebonyi State government. Recall that at the beginning of this month, I asked the Ebonyi State Government, led by Governor Francis Ogbonnaya Nwifuru, about the whereabouts of those aircraft. We just cannot continue in this manner. Our limited resources should be prudently utilized for the benefit of all Ebonyi people. N50bn is not a small amount of money to be forgotten just like that. Ebonyi people deserve to know what happened to those purchased aircraft or the said N50bn earmarked for the transaction.

“With N50bn, Ebonyi State will improve economically. If such money is invested in industries and agriculture, it will not only improve the Internally Generated Revenue, it will also provide jobs for our unemployed people in Ebonyi State. N50bn is not a small amount of money to be invested wrongly. In Abakaliki, people do not have good water to drink. In Afikpo North, there is no light, no good roads, no good primary and secondary schools, and no good hospitals in our 13 LGs. How can anyone expect Ebonyi people to be happy on hearing that N50bn cannot be accounted for? This is not acceptable. Something has to be done about it immediately.

“If I were an anti-graft agent, I would have invited all the people involved in this failed aircraft transaction for questioning. I cannot pretend that all is well when there are no aircraft seen on ground to justify the N50bn earmarked for that transaction. Honestly, if I were an anti-graft agent, all the people involved must be facing prosecution.”

The state government had not responded to inquiries from The PUNCH at the time of filing this report.

The former state Commissioner for Aviation Technology, Mrs. Ngozi Obichukwu, who was redeployed to the Ministry of Special Projects last week, said she was not yet ready to speak on the matter.

Messages sent to her mobile phone were ignored and not responded to.

However, when she eventually picked her calls, she told The PUNCH, “I am not ready yet to talk to you about this. When I am ready, I will call you and your colleagues to address you on this.”

Similarly, the state Commissioner for Information and State Orientation, Ikeuwa Omebe, followed the same pattern.

Initially, he neither picked his calls nor responded to several inquiries from The PUNCH for two weeks.

When our correspondent visited him in his office on Monday, he said he was yet to study the matter and asked to be given until Saturday, July 4 to respond to the newspaper’s inquiries.

He didn’t pick his calls on Saturday, but when he eventually did, he said, “I will find the time to reach out to you so we can talk.”

He was no longer picking calls on Sunday and had yet to reach out to The PUNCH for reactions or comments on the issue – as promised – at the time of filing this report.
